body.x: The Kyungnam University WISE LINC 3.0 Project Group (Director: Park Eunju) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 as part of the K-Startup Pavilion.

Guided by its vision to establish itself as an entrepreneurial university that inspires regional development through academia-industry collaboration, Kyungnam University is positioning itself as a leader in 21st-century education paradigms aligned with the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
The project group will showcase three innovative items developed by aspiring entrepreneurs supported by the WISE LINC 3.0 initiative at CES 2025.

The first is a scalp health diagnosis mobile application. This app allows users to assess their scalp condition easily at home by simply taking photos with their smartphone. The application provides instant analysis and personalized scalp care recommendations, utilizing advanced image recognition and analysis technology for an accessible and convenient self-diagnosis solution.

The second innovation is an AI-powered communication assistance app. Designed to enhance sentence and word recognition, the app surpasses traditional sign language recognition models by precisely understanding broader contexts. By analyzing actions and communication cues between frames and pixels, the app facilitates seamless and detailed interactions for users.

A diet management app leveraging AI and digital health technology will also be introduced. This app eliminates the need for manual food data entry, offering accurate nutritional information in real-time based on simple photo inputs. By integrating AI with digital health trends, the app provides a quick and precise method for users to manage their dietary habits.

A Kyungnam University WISE LINC 3.0 Project Group representative stated, “These innovative apps redefine convenience, accessibility, and accuracy in their respective fields.” The project group aims to use CES 2025 to demonstrate its commitment to fostering groundbreaking solutions that address evolving consumer and healthcare needs.

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
